corridor_notes: 央广网 (CNR) article dated 2025-01-17, titled '韩凯：建设防城港至东兴天然气支线管道', quotes Han Kai (Party Secretary/Director, Fangchenggang Development & Reform Commission) at the 2025 Guangxi 'two sessions' recommending the government build a Fangchenggang-to-Dongxing natural gas branch pipeline: '全长约40公里，总投资约8000万元' (total length ~40 km, total investment ~80 million RMB) -- both exact matches to GEM. This is explicitly framed as a legislative recommendation ('我建议加快建设...并纳入2025年开工计划', urging inclusion in the 2025 construction-start plan), consistent with GEM's Status='proposed'. No station names, specific townships, or a detailed alignment have been published -- this is pre-approval/pre-EIA, so only the two endpoint cities are sourced.
researcher_notes: Confirms the pilot pass's finding: this is a real, publicly-recommended proposal (not a phantom entry) but remains pre-approval as of the newest evidence (2025-01-17); no construction-start, tender, or EIA filing was found in this pass either, so no finer-than-city route detail exists to source yet. news.qq.com/rain/a/20250117A01W2T00 is the identical wire story re-syndicated same-day -- verified OK but does not count as a second independent source per the corroboration rule, so this stays medium-confidence on a single primary source (the CNR original). Coordinates are necessarily coarse (city-level) given the proposal stage; a route-creation pass should revisit once an approval/EIA names actual stations.
blockers: No station-level or township-level route detail is publicly available yet -- this is a legislative recommendation with no formal approval, EIA, or engineering filing found. Endpoint coordinates are city-level anchors, not a sourced alignment.
